framing: Keep your promises when a model goes down
paragraphs: In the last chapter you put a one-cent ceiling and a 300-token output cap on every generation. That single-call budget breaks the moment a primary model stalls. Sending a slow request twice spends twice, and falling back to an unrestricted public endpoint would violate data privacy and output schema rules in a single retry.

A model gateway enforces all of those constraints in one place. Rather than swapping models blindly by price, it checks tenant privacy scope, structured JSON support, citation conventions, human-review flags, and remaining deadline before dialing any backup endpoint.

Along the way you'll separate transport failures from semantic errors with an EWMA circuit breaker, propagate a shared request clock and spend cap across retries, and isolate idempotent tool writes from generation retries.
Every routing table entry here uses illustrative latencies and charges from our local test catalog rather than live vendor quotes.
outcomes: Filter model lanes by privacy scope, context size, and evaluated schema support before scoring latency or price
Track provider EWMA health, half-open recovery probes, and per-request deadline and budget ceilings
Keep post-generation validation and idempotent side effects separate from transport retries
question: If the healthy backup is cheaper and twice as fast, why might a gateway still reject it?
